properties.name: easygram.messaging.type
properties.description: Role of this application in broker integration. PRODUCER publishes Telegram updates to a broker; CONSUMER reads from a broker and dispatches to @BotController handlers. Omit for standalone bots.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.forward-only
properties.description: When true, updates are published to the broker only — local @BotController handlers are skipped. Only meaningful when messaging.type=PRODUCER.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.producer.type
properties.description: Broker backend for publishing Telegram updates. Required when messaging.type=PRODUCER.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.consumer.type
properties.description: Broker backend for consuming Telegram updates. Required when messaging.type=CONSUMER.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.topic
properties.description: Kafka topic name for publishing or consuming Telegram updates. Required when using Kafka.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.group-id
properties.description: Kafka consumer group ID. Used by consumer bots to identify their consumer group.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.create-if-absent
properties.description: Auto-create the Kafka topic on startup if it does not exist. Requires broker admin permissions.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.partitions
properties.description: Number of partitions for the auto-created Kafka topic. Only used when create-if-absent=true.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.kafka.replication-factor
properties.description: Replication factor for the auto-created Kafka topic. Only used when create-if-absent=true.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.rabbit.exchange
properties.description: RabbitMQ exchange name for publishing or binding the queue. Required when using RabbitMQ.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.rabbit.queue
properties.description: RabbitMQ queue name for consuming updates and auto-creation.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.rabbit.routing-key
properties.description: RabbitMQ routing key used when publishing messages to the exchange.

properties.name: easygram.messaging.rabbit.create-if-absent
properties.description: Auto-declare the RabbitMQ exchange, queue, and binding on startup if they do not exist.

values.description: Receive updates from Telegram and publish to a message broker. Long-polling or webhook transport is started.
Consume updates from a message broker and dispatch to @BotController handlers. No Telegram transport is started.
Publish Telegram updates to Apache Kafka.
